reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 a figurative constant written as a DISPLAY operand (ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES, SPACE/SPACES, HIGH-VALUE(S), LOW-VALUE(S), QUOTE(S), each with or without the redundant ALL, a symbolic-character with or without ALL) must be transferred as ONE occurrence, i.e. one character, and ALL literal as the literal once (IV-11 rules 2 and 3), wherever it stands in the operand list.

edition-consulted.switches: END-DISPLAY (EndDisplay2002) and a signed or fractional numeric literal operand (DisplayNumericLiteral2002) are refused at 85; neither touches a figurative operand
ResultLengthViolation(folded, edition.DialectLevel) on the folded literal-1 of ALL; the X"..", N".." and & forms of literal-1 are refused at 85 by their COBOL-2002 introduction gates (COBOL0900)

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior|Edition.Year over AcceptDisplayBinder.cs, AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs, OperandText.cs and CodeGen/Roslyn/FigurativeConstants.cs: none. The one-occurrence rendering (BoundFigurative -> new string(fill, 1); BoundAllLiteral -> the literal once) is the same code at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the DISPLAY probe's output is byte-identical at --std 85 and --std 2023 (diff p4.out p4_2023.out: SAME).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb243 covers ALL literal, ALL symbolic-character, bare symbolic-character, ALL ZEROES/SPACES/QUOTES; not covered there: bare ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE, HIGH-VALUE and LOW-VALUE, a figurative as the first or only operand, several figuratives in one statement, WITH NO ADVANCING

probes.expected: one occurrence of each figurative (IV-11 rule 2: length one), ALL literal shown once (rule 3)

probes.printed: H[U+FFFF U+FFFF][U+0000] for PIC X(2) VALUE HIGH-VALUE; DISPLAY HIGH-VALUE gives one U+FFFF
probes.expected: the bare figurative is one character of the same value an item filled from it holds

probes.printed: ALL X"41", ALL N"AB", ALL "A" & "B": COBOL0900 requires COBOL-2002; ALL "ZERO" prints [ZERO]
probes.expected: later-edition literal-1 forms refused at 85; ALL literal (permitted in DISPLAY from 1985) shown once

reader.notes: Every figurative form in a DISPLAY operand list was transferred once at --std 85. HIGH-VALUE shows as U+FFFF (UTF-8 EF BF BF), the same character an item filled with HIGH-VALUE holds; which character HIGH-VALUE is belongs to the collating-sequence rules and GR1's implementor-defined device conversion, not to this rule.

refuter.evidence: d1_hv.cob at --std 85 with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS STANDARD-1, a user alphabet, SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS SA IS 66 IN REV and DISPLAY ... UPON a CONSOLE mnemonic: every figurative is one character on both the default device and UPON (od: 'U[ ][0]["]'), SA and ALL SA one '>' (ordinal 66 of the REV alphabet, correct). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.10.4 GR3  (6.10.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3'. Reading noted, not overturning: under STANDARD-1 HIGH-VALUE still displays U+FFFF (EF BF BF), while §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 (cite.py: 'OK ... it lies in GR3') makes HIGH-VALUE the highest character of the program collating sequence; that is the value rule of IV.4.2.2.2.3(3)/the SPECIAL-NAMES rule (catalog rows of their own, and docs/rearchitecture/CODE-SPEC-AUDIT.md CA3 already records DISPLAY of HIGH-VALUE under a non-native PCS), not the single-occurrence count this rule governs. Side observation (not this rule): DISPLAY of a numeric PIC PP9 item holding .007 prints '.007' at 85 and 2023 (r3_pp9.cob), a DISPLAY-conversion question for GR1.
